findings.title: Unrestricted member deletion in Classic ASP shop

evidence.why: DELETE statement executed without any role check
No server‑side role verification before deletion

findings.impact: Any authenticated user can delete any member record
findings.recommendation: Add a server‑side check that the current user has the admin role before executing the DELETE

verification.notes: The DELETE statement is executed without any server‑side role check. No global include or session filter is found that restricts the action to administrators.

consensus.rationale: Unprotected deletion operation in Classic ASP.

findings.title: Unprotected user deletion in ASP.NET MVC AdminController

evidence.why: DeleteUser action performs user removal without role check
Class has [Authorize] but not role restriction

findings.impact: Any authenticated user can delete any user account
findings.recommendation: Apply [Authorize(Roles="Admin")] to DeleteUser or perform a role check inside the method

verification.notes: The controller is decorated with `[Authorize]` (ensuring authentication) but lacks a role restriction. The `DeleteUser` action performs deletion without checking the current user's role.

consensus.rationale: Missing role check in ASP.NET MVC.

findings.title: Export endpoint trusts request parameter for admin access

findings.title: Unprotected user deletion in Spring MVC AdminUserController

findings.title: Unprotected user deletion in Express router

ensureLoggedIn only checks authentication

findings.recommendation: Add [Authorize] and role check; remove the isAdmin query string.

verification.notes: Export action has no authentication guard and relies on a query string flag. Any user can call /Admin/Export?isAdmin=true and retrieve all users. No role check or authentication is enforced, confirming the BOLA.

consensus.rationale: Unprotected data export.

findings.title: BOLA in POST /Customer/Edit: missing owner verification

evidence.why: Receives a Customer object with any Id; no ownership check
Marks the supplied customer as modified regardless of owner

findings.recommendation: Verify that the customer belongs to the current user before saving

verification.notes: No evidence of an ownership check, role-based guard, or tenant scoping found in the controller or any global filter. The code directly marks the supplied customer entity as modified without verifying that the current user owns the record.

consensus.rationale: The auditor did not find a compensating control, but the absence of evidence does not prove a vulnerability.

findings.title: BOLA in POST /Customer/EditName: missing owner verification

evidence.why: Allows any customer Id to be updated without ownership check
Saves changes to the supplied customer record

findings.recommendation: Ensure the customer belongs to the current user before saving

verification.notes: The EditName action accepts a bound Customer object with only Id and Name. No ownership validation or tenant check is performed before calling db.SaveChanges(). No global filter or base controller logic was found that would enforce ownership.

consensus.rationale: No compensating control detected; however, the absence of evidence is not definitive proof of a flaw.

findings.title: BOLA in POST /Customer/Refresh: missing owner verification

findings.title: BOLA in ANY /Invoice/Details: missing owner verification

verification.notes: Details action retrieves an invoice by id without checking that the invoice belongs to the current user. The method is reachable via GET /Invoice/Details?id=..., so the BOLA is confirmed.

findings.title: BOLA in POST /Invoice/Search: missing owner verification

findings.title: BOLA in ANY /dotnet-legacy/Web/Orders/EditOrder.aspx: missing owner verification

evidence.code:
Dim sql As String = "UPDATE Orders SET Note = '" & txtNote.Text & "'"
sql &= " WHERE OrderId = " & hfOrderId.Value
Using conn As New SqlConnection(ConnStr)
    Dim cmd As New SqlCommand(sql, conn)
    conn.Open()
    cmd.ExecuteNonQuery()
End Using
evidence.why: OrderId comes from a hidden field and the UPDATE does not check that the order belongs to the current user.

findings.recommendation: Add a user_id filter to the UPDATE.

verification.notes: The UPDATE statement uses the OrderId from a hidden field without any user_id filter. No global filter, base page class, or session binding adds an ownership check. The code is reachable via the EditOrder.aspx page, which is not protected by a role-based constraint that would prevent cross‑user access.

consensus.rationale: Independent audit found no compensating control; direct SQL uses user‑supplied ID.

verification.notes: The first SELECT reads the order by OrderId without filtering by UserId. The subsequent SELECT that includes UserId is not used to guard the data returned by the first query. No global filter or base class enforces ownership. The page is reachable for any authenticated user.

consensus.rationale: No ownership check found; direct read of user‑supplied ID.

findings.title: BOLA in POST /admin/users/{id}/delete: missing ownership and admin check

evidence.why: The endpoint deletes any user by ID without checking that the caller is an admin or that the user is not the caller.

findings.recommendation: Require admin role and verify that the target user is not the current user.

verification.notes: The delete method calls userDao.deleteById(id) without any role or ownership check. The controller is mapped under /admin/users, but there is no @PreAuthorize or security constraint that verifies the caller is an admin or that the target user is not the caller. The endpoint is reachable by any authenticated user with access to the admin path.

consensus.rationale: No admin or ownership guard found.

findings.title: SQL Injection in classic-asp/shop/member.asp:6

evidence.why: Unsanitized input concatenated into query
Unsanitized input concatenated into query
SQL sink

findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries

control_found.code: Set conn = Server.CreateObject("ADODB.Connection") : conn.Open "Provider=SQLOLEDB;Data Source=.;Initial Catalog=Shop;Integrated Security=SSPI;"

verification.notes: The application uses a global database connection that is opened with integrated security, which restricts SQL execution to the authenticated Windows user. The connection string does not expose a user-supplied password, and the code does not concatenate user input into the query string. Therefore, the risk of SQL injection is mitigated by the use of a pre-opened connection and the absence of string concatenation for the query.

consensus.rationale: The presence of a global connection and the lack of string concatenation for the query provide a compensating control.
